_comment: Gatekeeper budgets. Appendix F sets these as MINIMUMS: raising them by mutual agreement is legal, lowering them is not (M#12). The values here are the floor, so they are always safe to propose.
_comment_gates: The three cumulative gates of PRD 7 §3.1, in order: daily quota, token bucket, DOS detector. Measured demand is ~0.5 RPM against a 30 RPM budget, so none of these should ever fire in a real match. They are insurance against our own bugs (M#29), not throughput management - which is why the DOS ceiling is set where only a loop can reach it.
_comment_burst: Token-bucket capacity C, the largest legitimate burst. One report plus its three retries is 4 calls; 5 leaves one spare. Anything larger is a loop, not a match.
_comment_quota: Daily ceiling. At most 10 counted matches (max_games_per_team) send one report each, so 50 is five times the entire tournament's legitimate traffic and still far below any figure Google would act on.
_comment_dos: Abnormal-pattern lock. 20 calls in 10 s is 120 RPM - 240x measured demand, and unreachable by a match played at one move per turn. Reaching it means our own code is looping, and the pipe locks entirely: one lost report is cheaper than a suspended account.
